subject.title: Bug: tools.deny does not hide skill_workshop from Codex deferred tools

question: Is source-path evidence enough to clear this security-sensitive `tools.deny` report, or should maintainers require a live Codex/app-server reproduction before closing or dispatching a fix?
rationale: The current shared code path appears to honor deny policy, but the report describes an observed live session leak and the item is already labeled for live reproduction, maintainer review, security review, and no new fix PR.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open until a live Codex/OpenClaw session or focused exact regression proves whether the remaining leak is real.

options.title: Accept source-path proof
options.body: Treat the current source inspection and commenter’s current-main check as enough to remove live-repro pressure and close or relabel the issue.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow repair
options.body: Override the no-new-fix-pr state and ask for a focused regression/fix on the config-to-dynamic-tool propagation path.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a live Codex/OpenClaw session or focused exact regression proves whether the remaining leak is real.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits place this person on both Codex dynamic-tool build/lifecycle and Skill Workshop prompt-routing surfaces.
